applications.description: Construction of 1no. warehouse for use within Class E(g)(iii), B2 and B8 including access and servicing arrangements, vehicle parking, refuse storage, landscaping and associated works.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within 3 years of permission date
conditions.text:
The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date on which the permission is granted.
Reason: In pursuance of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 0601 Rev P4, 0602 Rev P2, 0610 Rev P1, 0701 Rev P3, 0702 Rev P3, 1001 Rev P4, 1050 Rev P2, 1321 Rev P5, 2231-21-01 Rev C, 2235-21-10 S5 Rev P03, 2235-21-11 Rev P04 and 2235-21-12 Rev P01.
Reason: In the interests of proper planning and for the avoidance of doubt.

conditions.summary: Programme of archaeological evaluation, safeguarding and post-excavation reporting
conditions.text:
To assess and mitigate the impacts of development on significant archaeological remains:
A) Prior to any development works within the 'Area of Archaeological Interest' as set out on plan 0610 Rev P1, the applicant shall secure and have reported a programme of archaeological field evaluation works, in accordance with a specification and written timetable approved by the LPA.
B) Following completion of archaeological evaluation works, no development shall take place until safeguarding measures to ensure preservation in situ of important archaeological remains and/or further investigation have been secured and approved.
C) The archaeological safeguarding measures, investigation and recording shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed specification and timetable.
D) Within 6 months of the completion of archaeological works a Post-Excavation Assessment Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA.
E) The measures outlined in the Post-Excavation Assessment Report shall be implemented in full and in accordance with the agreed timings.

conditions.summary: Detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme (pre-commencement)
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The detailed drainage scheme shall be based upon the Drainage Strategy prepared by Hydrock dated 02.10.23 and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of without increase to flood risk on or off-site. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate that silt and pollutants resulting from the site use can be adequately managed to ensure there is no pollution risk to receiving waters. The drainage scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Oil and petrol interceptor/separator scheme (pre-commencement)
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until such time as a scheme to install oil and petrol separators has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The scheme shall be implemented as approved. The scheme shall: Be designed and constructed to have a capacity compatible with the area being drained; Be installed prior to the occupation of the development and thereafter maintained for the lifetime of the development; ensure clean roof water and vehicle washdowns and detergents do not pass through the interceptor(s).
Reason: To reduce the risk of pollution to the water environment.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures to be installed prior to development commencing
conditions.text:
No development shall commence until the tree protection measures as set out in drawing no. 2235-21-12 Rev P01 and within the Arboricultural Report have been installed. The protection measures shall remain in place for the duration of the construction and no works, storage or other activity shall take place within a protected area unless specifically identified within the Report. The development hereby permitted shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Updated landscape planting and management plan (pre-superstructure)
conditions.text: No development beyond the construction of foundations or above slab level shall take place until an updated landscape planting plan and a landscape management plan, incorporating full details of both hard and soft landscape works has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The planting plan must demonstrate that a native species hedgerow will be incorporated into the site and the management plan must detail how all the habitats on site will be established and managed. These details shall also include existing trees, shrubs and other features, planting schedules of plants, noting species (which shall be native species and of a type that will encourage wildlife and biodiversity), plant sizes and numbers where appropriate, means of enclosure, hard surfacing materials, and an implementation programme. All hard and soft landscape works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development.

conditions.summary: Verification report for surface water drainage system prior to occupation
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system (subject to conditions 4 and 5) and prepared by a suitably competent person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.

conditions.summary: Verification report for site remediation strategy prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to any part of the permitted development being occupied, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy by Hydrock dated 01/12/23 and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.
Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

conditions.summary: Off-site surface water drainage works to be secured and implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that demonstrates that off-site surface water drainage works are appropriately secured and protected and subsequently implemented prior to the occupation of the development.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved prior to installation (ILP GN 01/21)
conditions.text:
No external lighting shall be installed unless such details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall be in accordance with the Institute of ILP Guidance Note 01/21 The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions) and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. Details of operation hours should also be included. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved scheme unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation.
Reason: To protect the amenities of the surrounding area.

conditions.summary: External plant details and noise assessment to be approved prior to installation
conditions.text:
No external plant shall be installed at the site until full details of such plant together with an updated noise assessment that takes into account the specific noise levels of the plant has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The external plant shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved scheme unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation.
Reason: To protect the amenities of the surrounding area.

conditions.summary: Building to be constructed to BREEAM 'Good' standard with certification on first use
conditions.text:
The building hereby approved shall be constructed to BREEAM 'Good' Standard, or an agreed equivalent standard, and prior to the first use of the building the relevant certification shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority confirming that the required standard has been achieved.
Reason: In the interest of promoting energy efficiency and sustainable development.

conditions.summary: Remediation strategy for previously unidentified contamination discovered during development
conditions.text:
If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site in line with paragraph 174 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Piling/penetrative foundation methods require prior written consent and risk assessment
conditions.text:
Piling or any other foundation designs using penetrative methods shall not be permitted other than with the express written consent of the Local Planning Authority, which may be given for those parts of the site where it has been demonstrated by a piling risk assessment that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to groundwater. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution caused by mobilised contaminants in line with paragraph 174 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted to 0800–1800 Mon–Fri, 0800–1300 Sat, none on Sundays/Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
No demolition/construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday.
Reason: In the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: External finishing materials to match approved drawing 1321 Rev P5
conditions.text:
The new building hereby approved shall be constructed using the external finishing materials set out on drawing no. 1321 Rev P5.
Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Replacement of failed trees/shrubs within 5 years of planting
conditions.text:
Upon completion of the approved landscaping scheme, any trees or shrubs that are removed, dying, being severely damaged or becoming seriously diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced with trees or shrubs of such size and species as may be agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority, and within whatever planting season is agreed.
Reason: In the interests of the visual amenities of the area and encouraging wildlife and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charging points to be provided prior to first use and retained permanently
conditions.text:
Prior to the first use of the development hereby permitted, the electric vehicle charging points shown on approved drawing 0601 Rev P4 shall be provided and shall be retained permanently.
Reason: To ensure the provision and retention of electric vehicle charging facilities in the interest of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

conditions.summary: Car parking and cycle parking spaces to be kept available at all times
conditions.text:
The area shown on approved drawings 0601 Rev P4 and 0701 Rev P3 as car parking space and cycle parking space shall be kept available for such use at all times and no permanent development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any order revoking or re-enacting that Order) or not, shall be carried out on the land so shown or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access thereto; such land and access thereto shall be provided prior to the operation of the light industrial unit hereby permitted.
Reason: Development without adequate provision for the parking of cars is likely to lead to car parking inconvenient to other road users.

conditions.summary: Use restricted to Class E(g)(iii), B2 and B8 only
conditions.text:
The building shall be used in an industrial and/or storage use as defined by Class E (g)(iii), B2 and B8 and for no other purpose whatsoever, including any other purposes in Class E of The Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020 (as amended) and any other use whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any order revoking or re-enacting that Order) or not.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the amenity of the surrounding area.

applications.address: Chiplime House Beddow Way Aylesford Kent
applications.description: Division of existing site to form a new separate compound with the erection of 2no. warehouses including the new access, gates and parking.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years of permission date
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission;
Reason: In accordance with the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development to be carried out in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:
Application Form - Received 15/02/2024
Proposed Mezzanine Floor Plan - Drawing No. 24CC-090224-P-004 - Received 29/02/2024
Proposed Warehouse Plans and Elevations - Drawing No. 24CC-090224-P-006 - Received 29/02/2024
Proposed Ground Floor Plan, Site Location and Block Plan - Drawing No. 24CC-090224-P-003 - Received 29/02/2024
Proposed Site Elevations and Sections - Drawing No. 24CC-090224-P-005 - Received 29/02/2024
Reason: To clarify which plans have been approved.

conditions.summary: External materials to match approved plans and application form
conditions.text:
The materials to be used in the development hereby approved shall be as indicated on the approved plans and application form.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement archaeological field evaluation, investigation and publication
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of development hereby approved the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, will secure:
i. archaeological field evaluation works in accordance with a specification and written timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; and
ii. further archaeological investigation, recording and reporting, determined by the results of the evaluation, in accordance with a specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority;
iii. programme of post excavation assessment and publication.
The development shall only proceed in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined, recorded, reported and disseminated.

conditions.summary: Ecological enhancement scheme (swift bricks, bat/bee bricks, bird/bat boxes etc.) prior to occupation
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall not commence above slab level until details of a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through at least one integrated method into the design and appearance of the buildings by means such as swift bricks, bat tubes or bee bricks, and through the provision within the site curtilage such as bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the buildings and all features shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To enhance the ecology and biodiversity on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination: cessation of works, remediation plan and closure report
conditions.text:
If during construction/demolition works evidence of potential contamination is encountered, works shall cease and the site fully assessed to enable an appropriate remediation plan to be developed. Works shall not re-commence until an appropriate remediation scheme has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and the remediation has been completed. Upon completion of the building works, this condition shall not be discharged until a closure report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The closure report shall include details of: a) Details of any sampling and remediation works conducted and quality assurance certificates; b) Details of any post-remedial sampling and analysis; c) If no contamination has been discovered during the build then evidence (e.g. photos or letters from site manager).
Reason: In the interests of protecting the health of future occupants from any below ground pollutants.

conditions.summary: Construction hours limited to 0800–1800 Mon–Fri, 0800–1300 Sat, no Sundays or Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
No construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday. [see informative].
Reason: In the interests of neighbour amenity.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise rating level ≥5dB below background (BS 4142:2014)
conditions.text:
The rating level of noise emitted from the proposed plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of BS 4142 : 2014 Rating for industrial noise affecting mixed residential and Industrial areas) shall be 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved in accordance with ILP GN01 guidance
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Lighting, GN01, dated 2011 (and any subsequent revisions), and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and in the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Operational hours limited to 0730–1800 Mon–Fri, 0800–1300 Sat, no Sundays or Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
All activity in connection with the commercial use of the application site and building (including deliveries and despatches) shall only take place between 0730-1800hrs Mon-Fri and 0800-1300 hrs on Saturdays with no activity on Sundays or bank holidays.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: BREEAM 'Very Good' Post-Construction Review Certificate required prior to occupation
conditions.text:
No part of the development hereby approved shall be used or occupied until a Post-Construction Review Certificate issued by the Building Research Establishment or other equivalent assessors confirming that the development has achieved a BREEAM rating of not less than the standards equivalent to 'Very Good' has been submitted to and acknowledged in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources.

conditions.summary: Use restricted to Use Class B8 (Storage and Distribution) only
conditions.text:
The approved buildings shall only be used for warehouse purposes within planning use class B8 (Storage and Distribution).
Reason: The use of the buildings has only been considered in connection with the proposed use and other uses have the potential to result in amenity or highway impacts.

applications.address: Land At School Lane Church Lane Kent ME9 7JU

Alternatively, prior to the commencement of the approved use, information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that satisfactorily demonstrates firstly why the 'Very Good' standard cannot be met and secondly to show that the development achieves the maximum possible level of building sustainability.
Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources.

conditions.summary: Contamination: cease works if found, remediation plan required, closure report on completion
conditions.text:
If during demolition or construction works evidence of potential contamination is encountered, works shall cease and the site fully assessed to enable an appropriate remediation plan to be developed. Works shall not re-commence until an appropriate remediation scheme has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and the remediation has been completed. Notwithstanding the above paragraph and in any event, upon completion of the building works, this condition shall not be discharged until a closure report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The closure report shall include details of (a) Details of any sampling and remediation works conducted and quality assurance certificates... (b) Details of any post-remedial sampling and analysis... (c) If no contamination has been discovered during the build then evidence (e.g. photos or letters from site manager) to show that no contamination was discovered should be included.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the health of future occupants from any below ground pollutants.

In exceptional circumstances, such as areas with a very low background or where assessment penalties total above 5 the applicant's consultant should contact the Council's Environmental Protection Team (ehadmin@midkent.gov.uk) to agree a site specific target level. Any mitigation measures approved through this condition shall be implemented prior to first use of the plant and equipment and retained and maintained at all times thereafter.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain condition – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate 10% Biodiversity Net Gain
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the necessary 10% Biodiversity Net Gain can be achieved, and as such there is no evidence that a biodiversity gain condition is capable of being successfully discharged. The net loss of biodiversity would have an adverse impact on the character and appearance of the area and as such would be contrary to National Planning Policy Guidance, paragraph: 019, policies LPRSP9, LPRSP14A, LPRSP15, LPRINF3 and LPRQD4 of the Maidstone Borough Council Local Plan Review (2021-2038), as well as Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by Schedule 14 of the Environment Act 2021).

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate flood resistance and resilience of battery unit and solar panels
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the development is or can be reasonably made appropriately flood resistant and resilient and that the proposed battery unit and/or the proposed solar panels could remain operational during a flood event. The proposal is therefore contrary to paragraph 173 of the NPPF, and policies LPRSP9, LPRSP14A, LPRSP15, LPRINF3 and LPRQD4 of the Maidstone Borough Council Local Plan Review (2021-2038).

conditions.text: The use proposed falls within Class E (e) of the GPDO, however, the restriction imposed by condition 3 appended to the previous planning permission under reference number MA/14/0338 means the proposal is not permitted development. The application therefore fails to comply with Schedule 2 Part A of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (the UCO) as amended by the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020. A Lawful Development Certificate cannot be issued.

conditions.summary: Refusal: insufficient evidence of continuous 10-year B8 storage use
conditions.text: Submitted information is not sufficiently precise or unambiguous to determine on the balance of probabilities that the existing building has been used as a storage building under Use Class B8 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) for the 10 years preceding the application submission. Evidence indicates that there have been substantial breaks in the use of the site over the previous 10 years. During these breaks no breach appeared to be taking place and enforcement action could not have reasonably been taken at these times. As such, these periods do not contribute towards the rolling period of years that would otherwise contribute to immunity. For these reasons, this application for a Lawful Development Certificate (existing) is refused.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures (BS 5837) to be approved before works
conditions.text:
No further work shall take place until details of protection for trees and new areas of structural planting in accordance with the current edition of BS 5837 have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. All trees to be retained must be protected by barriers and/or ground protection. Nothing shall be stored or placed, nor fires lit, within any of the protected areas. No alterations shall be made to the siting of barriers and/or ground protection, nor ground levels changed, nor excavations made within these areas without the written consent of the local planning authority. These measures shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Retention of cut timber for saproxylic organisms
conditions.text:
All cut timber/wood between 15cm and 60cm in diameter, together with any senescent and rotting wood, should be retained and stacked safely on site for the colonisation of saproxylic organisms, except where an alternative proposal has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: In the interests of wildlife and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charging point per dwelling prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Each individual dwelling hereby approved shall not be occupied until a minimum of one electric vehicle charging point has been installed on its associated carport/wagon shed, and shall thereafter be retained for that purpose.
Reason: To promote the reduction of CO2 emissions through the use of low emissions vehicles.

conditions.summary: Programme of historic building recording before works commence
conditions.text:
No further work shall take place until the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, have secured the implementation of a programme of building recording in accordance with a written specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All works shall proceed in accordance with the approved measures.
Reason: To ensure that historic building features are properly examined and recorded.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan (routing, parking, deliveries, dust, wheel wash)
conditions.text:
No further works shall take place until a Construction Management Plan for the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Construction Management Plan shall include the following details- (a) Routing of construction and delivery vehicles to / from site (b) Parking and turning areas for construction and delivery vehicles and site personnel (c) Timing of deliveries (d) Provision of wheel washing facilities (e) Temporary traffic management / signage (f) Measures to control dust and potential use of asbestos in the existing building. The construction works shall proceed only in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and highway safety.

conditions.summary: Occupation limit – max 8 households and 16 occupants
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall have no more than 8(no) separate households, with no more than 16(no) occupants, occupying the building at any one time.
Reason: To protect the amenity of future occupants.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme (indigenous species) to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the accommodation hereby approved a scheme of landscaping, using indigenous species, together with a programme for the scheme's implementation, shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall include indications of all existing trees and hedgerows on the land to be retained and shall also include: (a) A landscape scheme designed in accordance with principles of Council's landscape character guidance (Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012); (b) Details of the number, size, species, maturity, spacing and position of proposed trees and landscaping to be planted on the site; (c) Measures to maximise soft landscaped areas on the site and reduce hardstanding areas including a reduction in the cycle parking shown on the submitted plans. (d) Evidence to show that hardstanding areas (including parking and service areas) are the minimum area necessary for their safe operation. (e) Measures (such as post and rail fencing) to prevent vehicles parking on soft landscaped areas, and (f) A ten year landscaping management plan. Only non-plastic guards shall be used for new trees and hedgerows, and no Sycamore trees shall be planted.
Reason: In the interests of visual impact and biodiversity enhancement.

conditions.summary: Approved landscaping to be carried out in first planting season and retained for 10 years
conditions.text:
All landscaping specified in the approved landscape details shall be carried out in the first planting season (1 October to end of February) following the first occupation of the development hereby approved. The approved landscaping shall be retained for at least 10 years following its implementation and shall be managed and retained strictly in accordance with the approved specification/management plan, and any approved or retained seeding or turfing which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, before a period of 10 years from the completion of the development has expired, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their amenity value has been adversely affected, shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of visual impact.

conditions.summary: Ecology enhancement details to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, details of ecology enhancements shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These details shall include identifying the location and height, and the make/specification of the enhancements; and the development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, with all features being maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of securing ecology enhancements.

conditions.summary: Secured by Design crime prevention details to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, details of how it has designed out crime (in reference to Secured by Design) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved details shall be in place prior to the first occupation of the of the development hereby approved and shall be maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of promoting safe and secure communities and environment.

conditions.summary: External lighting details to be submitted and approved prior to installation
conditions.text:
No external lighting, whether temporary or permanent, shall be placed or erected on the site unless details are first submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Submitted details shall: (a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Lighting, 01/21 - The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions) (b) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. (c) only include external lighting that is both low level and on motion sensors. The external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first use of the lighting. The lighting shall thereafter be operated, retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Bin storage facility to be installed and useable prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
The onsite bin storage facility, as shown on the submitted plans, shall be installed and fully useable prior to the first occupation of the building, and it shall be retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: 16 parking spaces and vehicle turning areas to be available prior to first use
conditions.text:
The approved details of the 16(no) parking spaces and vehicle turning areas shall be available prior to the first use of the development hereby approved and shall thereafter be kept available for such use. No development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order, with or without modification) or not, shall be carried out on the areas indicated or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to them.
Reason: Development without adequate parking/turning provision is likely to lead to parking inconvenience to other road users.

conditions.summary: Decentralised/renewable/low-carbon energy to meet at least 10% of annual energy requirements

The accommodation hereby approved shall not be occupied until details of how decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy will be incorporated into the development hereby approved to provide at least 10% of total annual energy requirements of the development, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved details shall be installed prior to first occupation of the approved accommodation and retained and maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure an energy efficient form of development.

conditions.text:
Prior to operation of the solar panels hereby approved, details of a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through the provision on site of bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and all features shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To enhance the ecology on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Landscape scheme to be approved and implemented prior to first operation
conditions.text:
Prior to first operation of the solar panels hereby approved landscaping shall be in place that is in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall
a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's Landscape Guidelines (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012).
b) show all existing trees, hedges and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site and indicate whether they are to be retained or removed,
c) provide details of additional native planting surrounding the solar panels as shown in drawing no. 24_03_P03 D.
d) provide a planting schedule (including location, planting species and size).
e) provide implementation details and a [5] year management plan.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual amenity and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Completion of approved landscaping and replacement of failed planting within 5 years
conditions.text:
All landscaping specified in the approved details shall be completed by the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first use of the solar panels hereby approved. Any of the approved landscaping which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, within five years from the first planting, are removed, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: External lighting details to be approved – ILP GN01 and BCT Guidance Note 8 compliance
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Professionals Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, GN01, dated 2011 (and any subsequent revisions)
b) follow the recommendations within the Bat Conservation Trust's 'Guidance Note 8 Bats and Artificial Lighting'.
c) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species.

conditions.summary: Removal of solar panels and restoration of land within 6 months of cessation of operation
conditions.text:
Within 6 months of the solar panels ceasing to be operational, they and all associated infrastructure shall be removed, and the land restored to its previous condition.
Reason: To ensure the long-term appearance and use of the land is preserved after the use ceases.

conditions.summary: Acoustic report addressing noise and low-frequency noise from solar facility prior to operation
conditions.text:
Prior to first operation of the solar panels hereby approved, an acoustic report assessing noise impact shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall address the issue of noise (including low frequency noise) and vibration from the facility to ensure that there is no loss of amenity to residential or commercial properties. For residential accommodation, the scheme shall ensure that the low frequency noise emitted from the equipment is controlled so that it does not exceed the Low Frequency Criterion Curve for the 10 to 160Hz third octave bands inside residential accommodation as described in The DEFRA Procedure for the assessment of low frequency noise complaints 2011 (NANR45). The equipment shall be maintained in a condition so that it complies with the levels and mitigation measures specified in the approved acoustic report, whenever it is operating. After installation of the approved plant no new plant shall be used without the written consent of the local planning authority.
Reason: In the interest of upholding high standards of neighbour amenity.

conditions.summary: Approved landscaping to be completed by end of first planting season after first use

Any of the approved landscaping which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, within five years from the first planting, are removed, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved prior to installation (ILP GN01 & BCT Guidance)

The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species.

conditions.summary: Removal of solar panels and restoration of land within 6 months of ceasing operation

Reason: To ensure the long-term appearance and use of the land is preserved after the use ceases.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise rating level ≥5dB below background LA90 (BS 4142:2014+A1:2019)

conditions.summary: Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) for ≥10% BNG over 30 years
conditions.text:

The HMMP shall: a. show a minimum of 10% onsite biodiversity net gain (submitted and approved through the Biodiversity Gain Plan) maintained for a period of 30 years from completion of the development; b. include a non-technical summary; c. include the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP; d. include the planned habitat creation and enhancement works; e. include the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years; and f. include the monitoring methodology with monitoring reports submitted on year 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30. Written notice shall be submitted to the local planning authority when habitat creation and enhancement works as set out in the HMMP have been completed.
Reason: To ensure measurable net gains to biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Refusal reason – harm to countryside, landscape and Kent Downs National Landscape
conditions.text: The proposed development would cause significant harm to the character and appearance of the countryside and landscape within the local area through its scale (extent of area covered), urban appearance, and prominence from public vantage points. It would also have a significant harmful impact on the Kent Downs National Landscape and therefore fail to conserve or enhance this National Landscape. This would be contrary to policies LPRSP9 (Parts 2 and 4) and LPRQD4 (Parts 1 and 2) of the Maidstone Local Plan Review, principles SD2, SD3, and SD5 of the Kent Downs AONB Management Plan, paragraphs 187(a) and (b) and 189 of the NPPF. The development would also fail to further the purpose of conserving or enhancing the natural beauty of the National Landscape as required under Section 245 of the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. The 40 year lifespan or benefits of the development are not considered to outweigh this conflict with the Development Plan or national policy.

conditions.summary: Refusal reason – exceptional circumstances not demonstrated for major development in National Landscape
conditions.text: Although the need for, and level of, renewable energy generation from the development is considered to be in the public interest, the development would have a minimal impact upon the local economy, the scope for developing outside the National Landscape has not been demonstrated as being unfeasible, it would have a harmful impact on the recreational enjoyment opportunity experienced on the North Downs Way National Trail, and it would cause significant harm to the Kent Downs National Landscape. It is therefore considered that exceptional circumstances have not been demonstrated to allow major development in the National Landscape contrary to paragraph 190 of the NPPF.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain condition – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text:
Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless:
(a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and
(b) the planning authority has approved the plan.
There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply. These can be found at: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2024/47/contents/made

conditions.summary: Detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme prior to commencement

The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate (with reference to published guidance): i) that silt and pollutants resulting from the site use can be adequately managed to ensure there is no pollution risk to receiving waters. ii) appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements for each drainage feature or SuDS component are adequately considered.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water and to ensure that the development does not exacerbate the risk of on/off site flooding.

The building or land shall be used for car repairs garage (Use Class B2) only and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Class B) of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or permitted under the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 or any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting those Orders with or without modification).
Reason: The information submitted with the application and the subsequent assessment of the available information has only considered the potential impact of the development shown as part of the submitted application and no other alternatives.

conditions.summary: Acoustic assessment, attenuation scheme and Site Development Scheme (BS4142)
conditions.text:
The use hereby approved shall cease and all associated material shall be removed within 28 days of the date of failure to meet any one of the requirements set out in (a) to (d) below:
(a) Within 3 months of the date of this decision a scheme, hereafter referred to as the Site Development Scheme, shall have been submitted for the written approval of the local planning authority. The Site Development Scheme shall include:
(i) An acoustic assessment and subsequent report to demonstrate that the rating level of noise emitted from any plant and equipment on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) is 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. Where the background sound level is below 30dB(A) or where assessment penalties total above 5dB the applicant's consultant shall contact the Environmental Protection Team to agree a site-specific target level.
(ii) Details of attenuation measures to meet the noise levels specified above.
(iii) A timetable for implementation of the agreed attenuation measures in the Site Development Scheme.
Reason: No such details have been submitted and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Maintenance of acoustic equipment and attenuation measures
conditions.text:
The equipment and attenuation required by condition 3 shall be maintained in a condition so that it complies with the levels and mitigation measures specified in the approved acoustic report, whenever it is operating. After installation of the approved plant no new plant shall be used without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: No such details have been submitted and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Impervious bunded storage for oils, fuels and chemicals (110% capacity)
conditions.text:
Any facilities used for the storage of oils, fuels or chemicals shall be sited on impervious bases and surrounded by impervious bund walls. The bund capacity shall give 110% of the total volume of the tanks.
Reason: To prevent contamination and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

Reason: To safeguard the characteristics of the building and locality and to ensure special regard is paid to the interests of protecting the special architectural and historic character detailing the integrity of the Listed Building under Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Building Conservation Areas) Act 1990.

Reason: To safeguard the characteristics of the building and locality and to ensure special regard is paid to the interests of protecting the special architectural and historic character detailing the integrity of the Listed Building under Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Building Conservation Areas) Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Chimney 04 works to accord with approved Schedule of Repairs

conditions.summary: Chimney 06 works to accord with approved Schedule of Repairs

The works to Chimney 06 shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Schedule of Repairs; Chimney 06 on page 11 of the Heritage Design and Access Statement received by the Council on 27/08/2025.
Reason: To safeguard the characteristics of the building and to ensure special regard is paid to the interests of protecting the special architectural and historic character detailing the integrity of the Listed Building under Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Building Conservation Areas) Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Development to begin no later than 30.09.2027
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun no later than 30.09.2027.
Reason: In accordance with the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development to be carried out in accordance with approved plans and documents
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents: Application form; BDS-VCH-SK100 Rev A; BDS-VCH-100; BDS-VCH-P03; BDS-VCH-P04C; BDS-VCH-P07; BDS-VCH-P08; BDS-VCH-P09; BDS-VCH-P01 Rev A; BDS-VCH-P02 Rev A; BDS-VCH-P04 Rev B; BDS-VCH-P05 Rev B; BDS-VCH-P06 Rev B; Affordable Housing Statement; Surface Water Drainage Strategy; Financial Viability Appraisal; Healthcare Viability Report; Renewable Energy Statement; Acoustic Report.
Reason: To ensure the quality of the development is maintained and to prevent harm to the visual amenity of the area.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan required prior to commencement
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall not commence until a Construction Management Plan for the development has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Construction Management Plan shall include the following details- (a) Routing of construction and delivery vehicles to / from site (b) Parking and turning areas for construction and delivery vehicles and site personnel (c) Timing of deliveries (d) Temporary traffic management / signage (e) Measures to control dust. (g) Measures to prevent the discharge of surface water onto the highway. The construction works shall proceed only in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and highway safety.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted: Mon–Fri 0800–1800, Sat 0800–1300, no Sunday/Bank Holiday working
conditions.text:
No demolition/construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday.
Reason: In the interest of the amenities of occupiers of neighbouring properties.

conditions.summary: External materials to be as indicated in Design and Access Statement
conditions.text:
The materials to be used in the development hereby approved shall be as indicated in the Design and Access Statement. The materials shall be permanently retained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: On-site ecology enhancement measures to be in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved the on-site ecology enhancement measures shown on drawing BDS-VCH-P08 (Biodiversity Site Plan) (received on 4th July 2024), shall be in place. All features shall be retained and maintained permanently thereafter.
Reason: To enhance ecology and biodiversity on the site.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme to be submitted, approved and implemented after first occupation
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the details submitted in Drawing number: BDS-VCH-P04C (Proposed Site Plan), at the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first occupation of any of the approved apartments landscaping shall be in place, that shall be in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscaping shall be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012). The landscaping shall include: a) Details of all existing trees, hedgerows, and blocks of landscaping; b) Details of number, size, species, maturity, spacing and position of proposed trees and landscaping; c) A timetable of implementation; d) A five [5] year landscape management plan.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Replacement planting required for failed or removed landscaping within five years
conditions.text:
Any landscaping which fails to establish or any existing or proposed trees or plants which, within five years from planting are removed, die, or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long-term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: External amenity space to be provided for all apartments prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved external amenity space shall be provided for all the apartments including: a) Direct access from the ground floor units b) Defensible space in front of all ground floor windows and c) Communal space accessible for the occupiers of the apartments at first and second floor levels d) The areas of approved amenity space shall be retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Management plan for open areas of the site to be submitted prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved a management plan, including management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for the open areas of the application site (excluding private amenity space) shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The approved management plan shall be followed thereafter.
Reason: To ensure the appropriate protection of wildlife and design of supporting habitat.

conditions.summary: Bin storage to be in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, the bin storage shown on the approved plans shall be in place. These details will be retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Waste collection strategy to be approved and in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, a waste collection strategy shall be in place that is in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The waste strategy shall set out arrangements for the collection of waste including the collection location and measures to ensure that bins are returned to the bin storage area. These details will be maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Minimum three Mode 3 SMART electric vehicle charging points prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, a minimum of three operational electric vehicle charging points for low-emission plug-in vehicles shall be installed on the site and ready for the use by new occupants with the electric vehicle charging points thereafter retained and maintained operational as such for that purpose. The electric vehicle charging points shall be provided to Mode 3 standard (providing up to 7kw) and SMART (enabling Wifi connection).
Reason: To promote sustainable travel choices and the reduction of CO2 emissions through use of low emissions vehicles.

conditions.summary: Decentralised/renewable/low-carbon energy sources to be incorporated prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, the decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy shown on drawing number: BDS-VCH-P09 (Sustainability Plan) shall be incorporated into the development hereby approved. The decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure an energy efficient form of development.

conditions.summary: External lighting details (layout, beam orientation, ISO lux plan) to be approved; bat conservation trust guidelines to be met
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The approved details shall be in accordance with bat conservation trust guidelines and the Institute of Lighting Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior Lighting Installations for Environmental Zone E1. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated thereafter in accordance with the approved scheme.
Reason: In order to prevent undue light pollution and to protect wildlife.

conditions.summary: Internal and external noise levels to comply with BS 8233:2014 prior to window installation
conditions.text:
Prior to the installation of any external windows a scheme to demonstrate that the internal noise levels within the residential units and the external noise levels in external amenity areas will conform to the standard identified by BS 8233 2014, Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings - shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The work specified in the approved scheme shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the any of the relevant apartments hereby approved and retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Crime prevention measures to be approved and in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, crime prevention measures shall be in place that are in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, with the approved measures retained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Car and cycle parking to be provided and retained prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, the car and cycle parking shown on drawing BDS-VCH-P04 Rev. B (Proposed Site Plan) (received on 23rd July 2023) shall be provided and ready for use, with the car and cycle parking retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interests of amenity and sustainable travel.

conditions.summary: Parking and turning areas to be completed and kept available; no development to preclude access
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the apartments hereby approved the parking and turning areas and cycle parking shown on drawing BDS-VCH-P04 Rev. B (Proposed Site Plan) (received on 23rd July 2023) shall be completed and thereafter shall be kept available for such use. No development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 or not, shall be carried out on the areas indicated or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to them.
Reason: Development without adequate parking/turning provision is likely to lead to parking inconvenient to other road users and in the interests of road safety.

conditions.summary: Water efficiency standard of 110 litres per person per day (Building Regulations Part G2) to be met
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall meet the higher level of water efficiency of 110 litres per person, per day as set out under the building regulations Part G2 or any superseding standard. The building shall not be occupied unless this standard has been met and this standard shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a sustainable form of development.

conditions.summary: All ground floor dwellings to meet Part M4(2) accessible and adaptable regulations
conditions.text: All the approved ground floor dwellings shall meet the accessible and adaptable regulations part M4(2) standard or any superseding standard. The ground floor dwellings shall not be occupied unless this standard has been met and the dwelling shall be thereafter retained and permanently maintained in accordance with this standard and in accordance with M4(2) drawing BDS-VCH-SK100 Rev A (Building Design Studio).

conditions.summary: Sustainable surface water drainage works to be approved and implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
None of the apartments hereby permitted shall be occupied until sustainable surface water drainage works have been implemented in accordance with details that shall have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. No apartment shall be occupied until all the works necessary have been implemented in accordance with the approved details. a) Provide information about the design storm period and intensity, the method employed to delay and control the surface water discharged from the site, including any requirement for the provision of a balancing pond and the measures taken to prevent pollution of the receiving groundwater and/or surface waters. b) Provide permeable surfacing for the parking area, including a scheme of maintenance. c) Include a timetable for its implementation in relation to the development; and, d) Provide a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interests of pollution and flood prevention.

conditions.summary: Post-occupation landscaping scheme to be submitted, approved and implemented
conditions.text:
At the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first occupation of the approved accommodation landscaping shall be in place that is in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscape scheme shall be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance. conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted to Mon–Fri 0800–1800, Sat 0800–1300, no Sundays or Bank Holidays

No demolition/construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday.

conditions.summary: Construction Method Statement to be submitted and approved prior to development

The approved Statement shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The Statement shall provide for: i. the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors; ii. loading and unloading of plant and materials; i. storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development; iv. the erection and maintenance of security hoarding; v. wheel washing facilities; vi. a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works.
Reason: In the interests of the amenities of the area and highway safety and convenience.

conditions.summary: Development to begin within three years of permission date
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of the permission.

Reason: In accordance with the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development to accord with approved drawings and planning statement
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall continue to be carried out only in accordance with the details shown on drawing no's: DHA 3661-01 - 07(consec) and planning statement ref: MB/AN.35300 October 2025.

Reason: To retain control over the use in the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Use restricted to osteopathic teaching clinic ancillary to European School of Osteopathy only
conditions.text:
The building and land shown outlined shown in red on drawing no: DHA/36991/01 shall only be used as an osteopathic teaching clinic ancillary to the European School of Osteopathy's use of the adjoining land and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Class F1 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or permitted under the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 or any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting those Orders with or without modification).

Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Site Development Scheme required: ecology enhancement, landscaping, boundary treatment and timetable
conditions.text:
The use hereby permitted shall cease and all equipment and materials brought onto the land for the purposes of such use shall be removed within 28 days of the date of failure to meet any one of the requirements set out in (a) to (d) below:
(a) Within 3 months of the date of this decision a scheme, hereafter referred to as the Site Development Scheme, shall have been submitted for the written approval of the local planning authority. The Site Development Scheme shall include:
(i) a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site; to include the introduction of a swift nest box or boxes under the eaves of the building.
(ii) details of a native landscaping scheme (designed in accordance with the submitted details and the principles of Council's Landscape Character Guidance and Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012), to include the planting of new landscaping to reduce the negative visual impact of the large area of hardstanding that currently forms the building setting.
(vi) a low wall with railings and a privet hedge along the site frontage and replacement of existing coping on the side boundary wall with ragstone coping; and
(vii) a timetable for implementation of the Site Development Scheme.
[Conditions (b)–(d) relate to appeal and implementation requirements if approval is refused or not determined within the prescribed period.]

Reason: To remove a negative feature in the Tonbridge Road Street scene, in accordance with the adopted London Road Character Assessment and in interests of ecology enhancement.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme details: design principles, existing features, new planting spec, management plan
conditions.text:
The landscaping scheme required by condition 4 shall:
(a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012)
(b) show all existing trees, hedges and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site.
(c) provide details of new on-site planting in a planting specification (location, spacing, species, quantity, maturity).
(d) provide landscape implementation details and timetable
(e) provide a [5] year landscape management plan

Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation by first planting season; 5-year replacement obligation
conditions.text:
All landscaping shall be carried out by the end of the first planting season (October to February) following approval. Within five years from planting, any landscaping which is removed, fails to establish, dies or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme unless the local planning authority gives written consent to any variation.

Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain condition – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text:
Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the 'biodiversity gain condition' which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless:
(a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and
(b) the planning authority has approved the plan.
There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

applications.address: The Trafalgar 10 - 13 Rushenden Road Queenborough Kent ME11 5HB
applications.description: Change of use of hotel (Class C1) and pub (Sui Generis) to 4no. residential dwellings (Class C3), including erection of single storey and first floor rear extensions and alterations to fenestration.

conditions.summary: Unjustified loss of community facility and visitor accommodation (pub/hotel viability)
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the existing public house and hotel are not viable, that there is no demand for their use, or that alternative community facilities or those designated as 'Principal Tourism Assets' could not operate from the site. The proposed development would therefore result in the unjustified loss of a community facility and visitor accommodation, contrary to policies CP1(9) and CP6 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Inadequate off-street parking provision contrary to SBC Parking Standards SPD
conditions.text: The proposal, by virtue of failing to provide adequate off-street vehicle parking in accordance with the Swale Borough Council Parking Standards SPD, would lead to an increase in on-street parking demand in a location where there is limited capacity to safely accommodate such additional pressure. This shortfall would likely result in indiscriminate or hazardous parking on the public highway, to the detriment of highway safety and the free flow of traffic. As such, the proposal is contrary to policies DM7 and Policy CP2 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and NPPF.

conditions.summary: Inadequate living conditions for future occupiers regarding noise and disturbance
conditions.text: The proposed development would fail to provide adequate living conditions for future occupiers with regards to noise and disturbance in conflict with policy DM14 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and the National Planning Policy Framework.
