conditions.summary: Landscape harm in High Weald National Landscape – major development not justified
conditions.text: The development would introduce an urban and utilitarian infrastructure to an area designated for its outstanding beauty, the High Weald National Landscape. The topography of the site and the vast Public Right of Way network that surrounds the site increase its visibility from public viewpoints and it is unlikely that this harm could be overcome with screening. The proposal constitutes major development and has not demonstrated that exceptional circumstances apply. The significant landscape harm that would occur is spatially and temporally significant and is not outweighed by the moderate benefits of the scheme. The proposal would conflict with policies LN3.1 and LN3.5 of the Cranbrook and Sissinghurst Neighbourhood Plan (2023), LE1 of the Benenden Neighbourhood Plan (2022), CP4 of the Tunbridge Wells Core Strategy (2010), EN1 of the Tunbridge Wells Local Plan (2006) and emerging policies STR8, EN1 and EN19 of the Tunbridge Wells Submission Local Plan (2021), as well as paragraphs 187 and 190 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2025).

conditions.summary: Insufficient information on construction/delivery traffic and highway safety
conditions.text: The application has failed to provide sufficient information relating to the management of delivery vehicles, details of construction traffic routing through Water Lane's junction with Attwaters Lane, design details of the proposed passing places and the land ownership they are in, information relating to HGV movements over nearby bridges, details of the proposed off-site compound, and automatic traffic surveys. Without this information it cannot be demonstrated that the proposal would not have an unacceptable severe impact on highway safety. The proposal is therefore contrary to policies AM5.6 of the Cranbrook and Sissinghurst Neighbourhood Plan (2023), T2 of the Benenden Neighbourhood Plan (2022), TP1 and TP4 of the Tunbridge Wells Local Plan (2006), and STR6, TP1, TP2, and TP6 of the Tunbridge Wells Submission Local Plan as well as paragraphs 44, 45, and 116 of the NPPF.

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate statutory 10% Biodiversity Net Gain requirement
conditions.text: The application has failed to provide adequate information relating to Biodiversity Net Gain. The documents submitted anticipate an increase of 138.51% to the habitat units, and 46.62% to hedgerow units on the site. The majority of this increase is through the creation of 10.58Ha of 'good' condition modified grassland, which is highly unlikely to be achievable. A revised biodiversity metric has been requested, or a detailed rationale for achieving 'good' condition modified grassland underneath the solar panels. The proposal therefore fails to demonstrate the proposal would deliver the statutory requirement of 10% Biodiversity Net Gain and is therefore unacceptable, contrary to policies LN3.1 of the Cranbrook and Sissinghurst Neighbourhood Plan (2023), CP4 of the Tunbridge Wells Core Strategy (2010), and STR 8, EN 9 and EN 14 of the Tunbridge Wells Submission Local Plan as well as paragraphs 187(d) and 192(b) of the NPPF (2024).

conditions.summary: Insufficient fire safety information for the solar/battery storage proposal
conditions.text: The application has failed to provide sufficient information relating to fire safety of the proposal. Without this information the proposal cannot demonstrate it would not have an adverse effect on health and safety. This is contrary to Policy EN1 of the Tunbridge Wells Local Plan (2006), Policy EN1 of the Tunbridge Wells Submission Local Plan (2021) and paragraph 102 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2025).

conditions.summary: Inadequate information on surface water pollution risk during construction
conditions.text: The application has failed to provide adequate information relating to surface water pollution. The Outlined Landscape and Ecological Management Plan does not satisfactorily account for the risk of pollution from silt, oils, chemicals, and other contaminants from the construction phase of the development. Without this information the application cannot demonstrate it would not have an unacceptable impact on the environment through pollution. The proposal is therefore contrary to policies CP4 of the Tunbridge Wells Core Strategy (2010), EN18 of the Tunbridge Wells Local Plan (2006), STR8, EN24, and EN25 of the Tunbridge Wells Submission Local Plan as well as paragraphs 8(c) and 187(e) of the NPPF.

conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of development, a scheme of avoidance, mitigation, and enhancement of biodiversity on the site shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The approved scheme shall take account of any protected species that have been identified on the site, shall take into account the recommendations of the submitted Preliminary Ecological Assessment and other Surveys and shall have regard to the enhancement of biodiversity generally. The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved proposals within it and shall be thereafter maintained in perpetuity.
Reason: To protect and enhance existing species and habitat on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Badger walkover survey to be carried out and submitted within three months prior to commencement
conditions.text:
In accordance with the recommendations of the Badger Activity Survey Report, a badger walkover survey of the site shall be carried out, and submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval, within the three months prior to commencement to check for any recent activity conclusive of badger presence.
Reason: To protect existing species on the site.

conditions.summary: Bat inspection/emergence survey required prior to removal of Gardener's Cottage roof
conditions.text:
In accordance with the Recommendations of the Bat Emergence and Re-Entry Surveys Report, if works to remove the Gardener's Cottage commence prior to May 2026, the results from a visual inspection to be undertaken by a suitably qualified ecologist shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. If works commence during or after May 2026, an updated inspection and dusk emergence survey shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The removal of any roof tiles will be carried out by hand under the supervision of a suitably qualified ecologist.
Reason: In the interests of safeguarding protected species.

conditions.summary: Use restricted to C2 (residential home) only
conditions.text:
The premises/site shall be used for C2 (residential home) use only and not for any other purpose whether or not in the same use class of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or any subsequent Order revoking or re-enacting that Order, or whether the alternative use is permitted by virtue of Article 3 and Schedule 2 Part 3 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (as amended) or any order revoking or re-enacting that Order.
Reason: Planning permission has been granted for the proposal because of the particular needs of the existing care home and the demand for the facilities to be provided by the proposal.

conditions.summary: Finished floor levels to have minimum 600mm freeboard above 1% AEP flood level
conditions.text:
Finished floor levels (FFL) for the building extension shall be set to have a minimum 600mm freeboard above the 1% AEP (1 in 100 years) flood level, including the climate change allowance, in accordance with the approved Plan Nos.: 1571 P010C and 1571 P011C.
Reason: In the interests of protecting future occupiers from flood risk.

conditions.summary: Site-specific flood warning and evacuation plan to be submitted prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of any part of the development hereby approved, a site-specific flood warning and evacuation plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority (LPA).
Reason: In the interests of protecting future occupiers in the event of flooding.

conditions.summary: Archaeological watching brief to be secured prior to commencement of development
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of development (excluding the demolition of the existing Cottage) the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, shall secure the implementation of a watching brief to be undertaken by an archaeologist approved by the Local Planning Authority so that the development works are observed and items of interest and finds are recorded. The watching brief shall be in accordance with a written programme and specification which has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined and recorded.

conditions.summary: Detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme to be submitted and approved prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of development (excluding the demolition of the existing Cottage and the commencement of construction of the development below ground level) a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The submitted scheme shall demonstrate compliance with the required technical standards at the time of submission and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of without increase to flood risk on or off-site. The detailed drainage scheme shall incorporate permeable paving and other attenuation devices, and discharge surface water at a rate not exceeding 2 litres per second.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water and to ensure that the development does not exacerbate the risk of on/off site flooding.

conditions.summary: Drainage Verification Report to be submitted and approved prior to occupation
conditions.text:
No hereby approved unit/bedroom shall be occupied until a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system and prepared by a suitably competent person, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.
Reason: To ensure that flood risks from development to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those risks to controlled waters, property and ecological systems.

conditions.summary: Internal and external noise level scheme (BS 8233:2014) to be submitted prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of development (excluding the demolition of the existing Cottage and the commencement of construction of the development below ground level) a scheme to demonstrate that the internal noise levels within the residential units/bedrooms and the external noise levels in garden and other relevant amenity areas will conform to the standard identified by BS 8233 2014 (Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings) shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The work specified in the approved scheme shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the premises and be retained thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be submitted and approved prior to commencement
conditions.text:
No external lighting shall be installed until a detailed scheme of lighting has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of the development. This scheme shall take note of, and refer to, the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Lighting, GN01, dated 2005 (and any subsequent revisions) and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained, and operated in accordance with the approved scheme.
Reason: In the interest of protecting the character and amenities of the locality, the amenities of adjoining residents, and to protect the appearance of the area/environment and wildlife from light pollution.

conditions.summary: Renewable energy technology details to be submitted and approved prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement, written and illustrative details for renewable energy technologies within the development (that could include provision of PV panels and air source heat pumps) shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details which shall be retained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory, energy efficient standard of development.

conditions.text:

conditions.summary: Detailed joinery drawings (1:5 or 1:1) required prior to window installation
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the details hereby approved, prior to the commencement of the installation of new windows within either new or existing openings, detailed drawings to a scale 1:5 or 1:1 of all new joinery shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include sections, mouldings and glazing bars to a scale of 1:1 or 1:2 and means of fixing glazing. Details of finishes shall also be included. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To maintain the quality of the development within the Conservation Area.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures to be observed throughout construction
Internal and external noise levels to comply with BS 8233:2014 prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (excluding the partial demolition hereby approved), a scheme to demonstrate that the internal noise levels within the residential units and the external noise levels in back garden and other relevant amenity areas will conform to the standard identified by BS 8233 2014, Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings - shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The work specified in the approved scheme shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the premises and be retained thereafter.
Reason: To protect the residential amenity of future occupiers of the residential unit(s).

conditions.summary: Vehicle parking spaces to be provided prior to first occupation and retained
conditions.text:
The area shown on the approved drawings as vehicle parking space shall be provided prior to the first occupation of any of the units, and shall be retained for the use of the occupiers of, and visitors to, the development, and no permanent development, whether or not permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order), shall be carried out on that area of land so shown or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to this reserved parking space.
Reason: Development without provision of adequate accommodation for the parking of vehicles is likely to lead to parking inconvenient to other road users.

conditions.summary: Bicycle and refuse storage to be completed prior to first occupation and retained
conditions.text:
The bicycle and refuse storage facilities shown on the approved plans shall be completed and made available for use prior to first occupation of the hereby approved, and thereafter retained.
Reason: To ensure the provision and retention of adequate off-street parking facilities for bicycles in the interests of highway safety and sustainability. In the interests of visual amenity and to facilitate waste collection.

conditions.summary: Details of new fencing/boundary treatments to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of any new proposed fencing/boundary treatments shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The boundary treatments shall then be erected in accordance with the approved details, and no further boundary treatments shall be erected unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the character and amenities of the locality.

conditions.summary: Retention and replacement of existing trees, hedges and hedgerows
conditions.text:
All existing trees, hedges or hedgerows shall be retained, unless shown on the approved drawings as being removed. All trees, hedges and hedgerows on and immediately adjoining the site shall be protected from damage for the duration of works on the site. Any trees, or parts of hedges or hedgerows removed without the Local Planning Authority's prior written consent or which die or become, in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority, seriously diseased or otherwise damaged within five years following contractual practical completion of the approved development shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable and, in any case, by not later than the end of the first available planting season, with plants of such size and species and in such positions as may be agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure the continuity of amenity afforded by existing trees, hedges or hedgerows.

The plan shall include but not be limited to examples such as hours of operation and delivery, control of noise from plant and machinery, noise from internal and external activities and refuse storage. The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details at all times.

Reason: In the interests of residential and visual amenity.

Reason: In the interests of protecting the character and amenities of the locality, and to control and regulate development on this site.
